Selected Work

Real-Time Pig Behavior Recognition and Tracking

Anonymized Engineering Case · Engineering Evaluation · Illustrative demonstration

Locate multiple pigs in barn video, link their trajectories and scope real-time recognition of standing, walking and lying.

Discuss a similar project Technical diagram

Industry problem and engineering challenge

Several pigs can occupy the same pen at once. Monitoring requires matching changes in position and behavior to each animal’s track. Overlap, crossing paths and similar appearances can break tracks or switch IDs. Lighting changes can also affect the video quality.

Technical approach and architecture

Implementation and deliverables

The engineering evaluation separates frame-level detection, tracking and clip-level action classification so reviewers can isolate misses, ID switches and action errors.

Outcome

The public scope covers a planned evaluation of behavior classification, individual tracking and streaming performance.

  • Output specification for multi-pig detections and track IDs
  • Annotation specification for action labels and their timing
  • Test plan for occlusion, ID switches and end-to-end latency

Validation and evidence

Hold out clips by pen or recording period. Evaluate ID switches, action classification errors and end-to-end latency across crossings, occlusion and lighting conditions.
